subject: Volume tiers & marginal breakpoints — request for glide-path pricing
messages:
From: Alex Hemmings <alex.hemmings@finwell.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Samira Khan <samira.khan@finwell.com>, procurement@finwell.com
Date: Sat, 01 Aug 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood pricing model questions + usage deck attached

Hey Ben,

Thanks again for the product walkthrough last week — Samira and I ran your latency/cost numbers by our platform team and we want to start getting concrete on pricing for the hosted API. I attached our Q3/Q4 usage forecast to give you a sense of scale. Key asks from procurement:

- Can you confirm whether Redwood’s volume discounts are applied on a marginal breakpoint basis (each additional token at the lower rate after a breakpoint) or as a blended effective rate across all tokens?
- If marginal, can you provide an example ladder with breakpoints and per-token rates for our expected volumes?
- If blended concessions are possible, what concessions would you offer for a 12-month commit?

Our rough forecast (monthly average by quarter) is in the spreadsheet, but short version: Q3 avg ~400B tokens/month, Q4 avg ~700B tokens/month. We’re trying to model a glide-path where we increase commitment over the year and would like to understand the financial impact both under marginal and blended structures.

Can we get a written example we can show procurement and finance? Bonus if you can include both a marginal ladder and a blended option for comparison.

Thanks,

Alex
Alex Hemmings
Director, Procurement
FinWell Financial

Attachment: FinWell_usage_forecast_Q3-Q4.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Hemmings <alex.hemmings@finwell.com>
Cc: Samira Khan <samira.khan@finwell.com>
Date: Sun, 02 Aug 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood pricing model questions + usage deck attached

Alex — really appreciate the forecast, that’s super helpful. Short answers up front:

- By default our public hosted pricing is implemented as marginal breakpoints (each token is billed at the rate for the bracket it falls in). That’s the most transparent and predictable for variable workloads.
- We can offer blended effective pricing for committed deals — typically customers request blended when they want a single unit price for budgeting. Blended requires an explicit commit term and is usually priced slightly higher than the marginal-weighted effective price for the same total volume because it reduces our upside on growth.

I attached a quick stylized example (redwood-pricing-glidepath-v2.pdf) and sketched two short examples below using your forecast numbers. These are illustrative; if you like one direction I can formalize with exact token math and a term sheet.

Option A — Marginal ladder (default):
- 0 - 100B tokens/mo: $0.000020 per token
- 100B - 400B tokens/mo: $0.000012 per token
- 400B - 1T tokens/mo: $0.000008 per token
Notes: If you hit 700B in a month, the first 100B are billed at $0.000020, next 300B at $0.000012, and the remaining 300B at $0.000008.

Option B — 12‑month blended commit (example):
- Commit: 500B tokens/mo average for 12 months
- Blended price: $0.0000115 per token across the committed volume
- Overage: marginal rates apply above the committed volume
Notes: Blended simplifies finance reporting and can include a guaranteed uplift in utilization to get the blended rate.

A few clarifying Qs that will help produce a formal proposal:
- Is FinWell looking for a guaranteed committed token volume (monthly average) or just a capped discount ladder without a formal spend commit?
- Do you need quarterly true-ups or monthly reconciliation?
- Are there any compliance / audit requirements (SOC2, retention) we should factor into commercial concessions?

If useful I can do a 30-minute call with procurement + Samira and bring our pricing lead; happy to walk through the math.

Best,

Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood-pricing-glidepath-v2.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Alex Hemmings <alex.hemmings@finwell.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Samira Khan <samira.khan@finwell.com>, procurement@finwell.com
Date: Wed, 05 Aug 2026 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood pricing model questions + usage deck attached

Thanks Ben — that’s helpful. Quick clarifications from our side:

- Procurement prefers a blended price for budgeting simplicity, but Samira wants to see the marginal comparison side-by-side to understand upside/penalty dynamics.
- We’d be open to a 12-month commit with quarterly true-ups. Ideal glide-path for us would be: Q3 average 400B/mo, Q4 average 700B/mo, Q1 (next year) 900B/mo — so the yearly average would be ~700B/mo.
- Compliance: we will need SOC 2 Type II evidence and basic audit logs for usage; nothing else unusual at the moment.

Please prepare: 1) a marginal ladder example using the ranges you suggested, 2) a blended-priced commit tailored to a 12-month term that targets a 700B/mo average, and 3) a short note on how overage billing would work and true-ups. If you can return an example Excel with the math that procurement/finance can plug into their model, that would speed review.

Appreciate it.

Alex

Attachment: none

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2026 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Volume tiers & marginal breakpoints — need input on blended concession

Marissa / Laura — forwarding FinWell thread. Bottom line: they want a blended price for a 12-month commit targeting ~700B tokens/mo average, but procurement also wants the marginal ladder comparison. They flagged SOC2 and quarterly true-ups.

Two commercial options I think we can propose (please weigh in):

Option 1 — Stick to marginal ladder (no blended concession):
- Maintain marginal breakpoints as previously shared.
- Offer professional services credit for SOC2 evidence collection (small concession) and 60-day implementation credit.
- Upside: protects our tail if usage skews higher; simpler to align with published pricing.
- Downside: purchaser resistance from FinWell finance who want a single budget line.

Option 2 — Limited blended concession for 12 months:
- Commit: 700B token/mo blended for 12 months (quarterly true-ups).
- Blended price example: $0.0000109/token across committed volume.
- Overage above committed monthly volume billed at marginal overage schedule (same breakpoints).
- We ask for an annualized minimum ARR target (approx $9M-$12M range depending on exact blended).
- Upside: easier to close quickly and gives procurement the predictability they want.
- Downside: slightly compresses margin; we should require quarterly min checks and set a collar on net new usage that would materially change economics.

Questions for leadership:
- Is the blended price above (0.0000109) acceptable as a standard concession for an enterprise first-year commit for this profile?
- Any preference on the ARR floor we should push for given the region and expected adoption?

If you prefer, I can prepare a formal one-pager showing margin exposure under both options (simple P&L for FY27) and a short recommendation.

—Ben

> Thanks Ben — that’s helpful. Quick clarifications from our side:

> - Compliance: we will need SOC 2 Type II evidence and basic audit logs for usage; nothing else unusual at the moment.

Attachment: redwood-blended-example-20260810-draft.xlsx (internal spreadsheet)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Hemmings <alex.hemmings@finwell.com>
Cc: Samira Khan <samira.khan@finwell.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Aug 2026 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Volume tiers & marginal breakpoints — request for glide-path pricing

Alex — thanks for the clarity and the glide-path target. We ran two concrete scenarios and attached an Excel that lays out the month-by-month math so procurement can plug numbers into their model. High-level summary below.

Scenario 1 — Marginal ladder (transparent billing):
- Brackets (example): 0-100B: $0.000020; 100-400B: $0.000012; 400-1T: $0.000008
- If your monthly average is 700B for a month, the blended effective cost for that month ~ $0.0000100/token (weighted marginal math).
- Quarterly true-ups reconcile against committed targets if you choose any reserved capacity option.

Scenario 2 — 12‑month blended commit (FinWell preference):
- Commit target: 700B tokens/month average for 12 months (quarterly true-ups).
- Proposed blended rate: $0.0000109 per token across committed volume.
- Overage: any token above the committed monthly volume billed using the marginal overage schedule (same brackets as above).
- SOC2: we can include SOC2 evidence deliverables in the contract and provide an implementation credit to offset some validation work.

Recommendation and ask:
- If FinWell signs a 12-month commit at 700B/mo blended we can hold the blended price for the term and include quarterly usage true-ups. We’d like a 45-day signing window and a target ARR floor of $10M for the first year that will determine executive approval levels.

Next steps:
1) I’ve attached redwood-blended-example-20260815.xlsx with the month-by-month math and a side-by-side marginal vs blended P&L.
2) If that looks acceptable I’ll draft a scoped commercial term sheet (non-binding) that includes the blended price, quarterly true-up cadence, SOC2 deliverable dates, and the proposed ARR floor.
3) Suggest a short sync next week with procurement + finance to walk through the excel.

Let me know which option FinWell prefers and if you want redlines in a single doc we can move to a short-term non-binding LOI.

Best,

Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0199

Attachment: redwood-blended-example-20260815.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)
